paragraphs.text: Or, for the afflicted, made by Daniel, or some other prophet, not long before the return out of Babylon, where they suffered much but prayed little, as Daniel confesseth, Dan 9:13. Here, therefore, they are taught to take unto them words, and say, "Hear my prayer, O Lord," &c. In greatest afflictions there is place left for prayer, Psa 130:1, and something God will yield to it, when most bitterly bent against a people, Mat 24:20-21.
paragraphs.anchor: A Prayer of the afflicted

paragraphs.text: Pressed out of measure above strength, 2Co 1:8, ad deliquium animae, till heart faint and faith seem to fail, bowing down through weight of grief, ac si pars una corporis alia esset operta; for so the word here used signifieth, saith Kimchi, as if one part of the body were overcovered with another. Estque pulchra collatio in verbis gnataph et shaphac, quae naturam fidei depingunt, saith Mollerus; faith may be under a cloud for a season, but it will recover, and pour out its complaint before the Lord.
paragraphs.anchor: When he is overwhelmed

paragraphs.text: O Lord Christ, for so this psalm is to be understood, as the apostle showeth, Heb 1:6
paragraphs.anchor: Hear my prayer, O Lord

paragraphs.text: Which is, that thou wouldest be pleased to bring us poor exiles back to our own country; and so this prayer is answerable to that of Dan 9:1-27
paragraphs.anchor: And let my cry

paragraphs.text: For this would be worse than all the rest. See Jer 16:13, "I will cast you out of this land, and I will show you no favour." This last was a cutting speech, and far worse than their captivity; and yet,
paragraphs.anchor: Hide not thy face from me

paragraphs.text: Non exul curae dicitur esse Deo.
Festina, responde. In our earnest prayers we may press for expedition in general, not tying God to any particular time, as those Bethulians did in the Book of Judith.
paragraphs.anchor: Answer me speedily

paragraphs.text: Which the higher it mounteth the sooner it vanisheth. Some read it, in the smoke. So Psa 119:83, "I am become like a bottle in the smoke," dried and withered, exsuccus et exsanguis.
paragraphs.anchor: For my days are consumed like smoke

paragraphs.text: Ossa mea quasi frixa contabuerunt. My strength is gone, Veluti sartagines (Arab.). Here, to the twelfth verse, is a most lively picture of a dejected person, such as can hardly be paralleled; teaching us to be deeply affected with the Church’s afflictions.
paragraphs.anchor: And my bones are burnt as an hearth

paragraphs.text: Blasted with thine indignation, that ventus urens et exsiccans.
paragraphs.anchor: My heart is smitten

paragraphs.text: I am stomachless, through want of that heat that my heart should supply.
paragraphs.anchor: So that I forget to eat my bread

paragraphs.text: A broken spirit drieth the bones, Pro 17:22, and, by drinking up the marrow and radical moisture, casteth all into a consumption.
paragraphs.anchor: By reason of the voice of my groaning

paragraphs.text: Or bittern, which liveth in lonely places, and crieth out dolefully, Isa 34:11 Zep 2:14.
paragraphs.anchor: I am like a pelican

paragraphs.text: Avis lucifuga, a night bird, a night raven, the Vulgate hath it; others, a bat, a cuckoo, but mostly an owl, that noctis monstrum, as Pliny, lib. 10, cap. 12, speaketh of her, nec cantu aliquo vocales sed gemitu, hated of all other fowls, which never come near her, but to keep a wondering at her.
paragraphs.anchor: I am like an owl in the desert

paragraphs.text: I can as little sleep as eat, Psa 102:4. That nurse of nature, and sweet parenthesis of men’s griefs and cares, sleep, departeth from me,
paragraphs.anchor: I watch

paragraphs.text: Nec membris dat cura soporem.
That hath lost his mate, so have I mine associates, which is a sore loss, for optimum solatium sodalitium.
paragraphs.anchor: And am as a sparrow

paragraphs.text: This is an evil that man’s nature is most impatient with. See Psal. cxxxvii.
paragraphs.anchor: Mine enemies reproach me all the day

paragraphs.text: That let fly at me, or that once praised me, flattered me. So the Sept.
paragraphs.anchor: And they that are mad against me

paragraphs.text: Have sworn my death, or do swear and curse by me, as the Turks do at this day, when, to confirm a truth, they say, Iudaeus sim si fallam, I would I were a Jew, it is so. See Zec 8:13 Isa 6:11-13 Jer 29:22. God make thee as Ahab, and as Zedekiah, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: Are sworn against me

paragraphs.text: Being cast on the ground as a mourner, I know not whether I eat bread or dust; this relisheth to me as well as that, my mouth is so out of taste.
paragraphs.anchor: For I have eaten ashes like bread

paragraphs.text: I forbare not to weep, no, not while I drank; for tow is dry, and wine driveth away sorrow, we say; not so from me. Wine is called by Simonides in Athenaeus αμυντωρ δυσφροσυναων, an expeller of sadness.
paragraphs.anchor: And mingled my drink with weeping

paragraphs.text: This lay heavier upon the good man’s heart than all the rest, God was displeased.
paragraphs.anchor: Because of thine indignation

paragraphs.text: That is, that I might fall with the greater poise. Significatur gravissima collisio. De coelo in terram (R. Solom.). Here the prophet accuseth not God of cruelty, but bewaileth his own misery. Miserum est fuisse felicem, It is no small unhappiness to have been happy.
paragraphs.anchor: For thou hast lifted me up, and cast me down

paragraphs.text: As at sunset the shadows are at longest, but not longlasting.
paragraphs.anchor: My days are like a shadow that declineth

paragraphs.text: Mown down, and laid a drying.
paragraphs.anchor: And I am withered like grass

paragraphs.text: And therefore we, thy covenanters, shall be restored, Lam 5:19.
paragraphs.anchor: But thou, O Lord, shalt endure for ever

paragraphs.text: Which thou hast of us, and we of thee.
paragraphs.anchor: And thy remembrance

paragraphs.text: This he speaketh with as much confidence as if he had been in God’s bosom; for he knew the promise of deliverance after 70 years’ captivity. See the like Hab 1:12.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt arise and have mercy upon Zion

paragraphs.text: This he understood by books, as Dan 9:2, and therefore presseth God to a speedy performance. God loveth to be burdened with his own word, to be sued upon his own bond, &c. But besides the promise, the psalmist had another ground of his confidence, and that is in the next.
paragraphs.anchor: For the time to favour her, &c.

paragraphs.text: They pity her, and wish her welfare; much more then dost thou. He argueth from that sweet, tender, melting frame of spirit that was found in the faithful, which is but a reflex of that far sweeter that is in God.
paragraphs.anchor: For thy servants take pleasure in her stones

paragraphs.text: The ruins and the rubbish, heartily desiring and expecting a re-edification and restoration, whereof they had a sweet promise, Amo 9:9, and for the spiritual temple to be built of Jews and Gentiles, they had many more. See all that followeth.
paragraphs.anchor: And favour the dust thereof

paragraphs.text: By the restoration of Jerusalem, where the Messiah was to be born and manifested, the everlasting gospel shall be preached, and the Gentiles converted to the faith.
paragraphs.anchor: So the heathen shall fear, &c.

paragraphs.text: Caught by those fishermen, and their successors in the ministry.
paragraphs.anchor: And all the kings of the earth

paragraphs.text: Isaiah had foretold that the second temple should be more glorious than the first, Isa 54:11; Isa 60:17, the stones whereof were types of those living stones whereof that spiritual temple was to be built, 1Pe 2:5, and wherein God would manifest more of his glory than ever he had done in all the world besides.
paragraphs.anchor: When the Lord shall build up Zion

paragraphs.text: Heb. of the poor shrub that is in the wilderness, trod upon by beasts, unregarded, worthless; heath, juniper, wild tamarisk, Humilesque myricae (Virg.). Tremellius rendereth it Nudatissimi; others Excitantis se, the prayer of one that stirreth up himself to take hold of God, and thereby prevaileth with him. I came for thy prayer, saith the angel to Daniel, Psa 10:12.
paragraphs.anchor: He will regard the prayer of the destitute

paragraphs.text: This, that the poor shrub hath sped so well in prayer, together with all other the particulars of this psalm, and indeed the whole Scripture, Rom 15:4. So little truth is there in that assertion of the Jesuits, that the epistles of the apostles were intended only for the use of those Churches or persons to whom they were first written.
paragraphs.anchor: This shall be written for the generation to come

paragraphs.text: "Created in Christ Jesus unto good works," Eph 2:10, his regenerated people; for God planteth the heavens, and layeth the foundations of the earth, that he may "say to Zion, Thou art my people," Isa 51:16.
paragraphs.anchor: And the people which shall be created

paragraphs.text: This is no small condescension, since he abaseth himself to look upon things in heaven, Psa 113:6.
paragraphs.anchor: For he hath looked down from the height, &c.

paragraphs.text: That is, his poor despised servants, that are in themselves no better than the earth they tread on.
paragraphs.anchor: From heaven did the Lord behold the earth

paragraphs.text: Those prisoners of hope held so long captive in Babylon, the cruelty whereof is graphically described, Jer 51:34.
paragraphs.anchor: To hear the groaning of the prisoner

paragraphs.text: This shall be the business of the converted Gentiles, to make up one catholic Church with the Christian Jews, and to bear a part in setting forth God’s worthy praises. See Psa 102:18.
paragraphs.anchor: To declare the name of the Lord in Zion

paragraphs.text: sc. To the Lord Christ; for to "Shiloh shall be the gathering of the people," Gen 49:10.
paragraphs.anchor: When the people are gathered together

paragraphs.text: As they did under Constantine the Great, Valentinian, Theodosius, which three emperors called themselves vasallos Christi (as Socrates reporteth), the vassals of Christ: and the like may be said of other Christian kings and princes since, who have yielded professed subjection to the gospel, and cast their crowns at Christ’s feet.
paragraphs.anchor: And the kingdoms to serve the Lord

paragraphs.text: This is the complaint of the poor captives yet undelivered, In via, hoc est in vita, quia hic sumus viatores, in coelo comprehensores, here we are but on our way to heaven, and we meet with many discouragements.
paragraphs.anchor: He weakened my strength in the way

paragraphs.text: viz. According to my account; for otherwise in respect of God our days are numbered.
paragraphs.anchor: He shortened my days

paragraphs.text: Stat sua cuique dies.

Heb. Make me not to ascend, Serus in coelum redeam. Fain I would live to see those golden days of redemption. Abraham desired to see the day of Christ, Joh 8:56; Simeon did, and then sang out his soul. All the saints after the captivity looked hard for the consolation of Israel.
paragraphs.anchor: Take me not away in the midst of my days

paragraphs.text: And that is the comfort of thy poor covenanters, who are sure to participate of all thy goods.
paragraphs.anchor: Thy years are throughout all generations

paragraphs.text: Here is a clear proof of Christ’s eternity, Heb 1:10, because he was before the creation of the world, and shall continue after the consummation thereof, Psa 102:26-27. So the saints a parte post. 1Jn 2:17, "The world passeth away, and the lusts thereof; but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever."
paragraphs.anchor: Of old thou hast laid the foundation, &c.

paragraphs.text: i.e. They shall change form and state, being dissolved by the last fire, 2Pe 3:7; 2Pe 3:10.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall perish

paragraphs.text: Heb. stand, and with thee thy Church, Mat 22:32.
paragraphs.anchor: But thou shalt endure

paragraphs.text: Which weareth in the wearing; so do the visible heavens and the earth, whatever some write de constantia naturae. Isaiah saith it rotteth as a book (that is venerandae rubiginis), and wasteth away as smoke, Isa 65:17; Isa 66:22.
paragraphs.anchor: Yea, all of them shall wax old as a garment

paragraphs.text: The Greek hath roll them: confer Isa 34:4, ελιξεις αλλαξεις.
paragraphs.anchor: As a vesture shalt thou change them

paragraphs.text: Tu es tu (Arabic). Therefore immutable, because eternal, ut nihil tibi possit accedere vel decidere,
paragraphs.anchor: But thou art the same

paragraphs.text: By virtue of the covenant, and that union with thee which is the ground of communion. If it could be said of Caesar, that he held nothing to be his own that he did not communicate to his friends, how much more of Christ! Propterea bene semper sperandum, etiamsi omnia ruant. The Church is immortal and immutable.
paragraphs.anchor: The children of thy servants shall continue
